CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
Dear Shareholders,
As DLF marks 80 years, we celebrate a defining milestone. Founded in 1946 at the dawn of India’s 
independence, our journey has closely aligned with the nation’s growth. As India advances towards its 
centenary, we reaffirm our commitment to national progress and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 as 
articulated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister.
For eight decades, our journey has been anchored in trust, quality and innovation. Our success would not 
have been possible without the confidence and trust shown by our customers, employees, shareholders 
and the continued support of the Government.
DLF has played a key role in transforming India’s urban landscape, creating world-class developments 
and landmarks across leading cities. With a strong legacy, robust governance and institutional strength, 
DLF is well positioned for the next phase of growth. 
Looking ahead, we see strong opportunities in a resilient and growing India. Under the leadership of 
Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, the country has navigated global challenges while maintaining 
strong macroeconomic fundamentals. With continued focus on infrastructure and urbanisation, DLF stands 
committed to unlocking significant opportunities for India’s urban development.
Our commitment to inclusive growth continues through the social, educational and sustainability 
initiatives of the DLF Foundation.
I thank our Board for its guidance and remain confident in our ability to build on our legacy, seize 
opportunities and shape the future of urban India with purpose and resilience, creating lasting value for 
all stakeholders.
With best wishes,
Sincerely,
Rajiv Singh

Financial Performance Review and Analysis
The Company delivered a strong financial 
performance during the period. Consolidated 
revenue (including other income) grew to 
` 9,816 crore, delivering a 9% growth, as compared 
to the previous year. The Company’s operational 
performance remained robust with record collections 
of ` 13,517 crore backed by high collection efficiency 
across all our projects. As a direct outcome of strong 
cash generation, your Company has achieved its 
goal of zero gross debt in the development business 
ahead of the estimated timelines and consequently 
operates with a further strengthened balance sheet. 
Consolidated EBITDA stood at ` 3,070 crore. Your 
Company recorded a total comprehensive income 
of ` 4,408 crore during the year as compared to 
` 4,356 crore in the previous year.
DLF Cyber City Developers Limited
DLF Cyber City Developers Limited (DCCDL) 
reported a consolidated total income of ` 7,393 
crore, reflecting 15% growth over the previous 
period, primarily led by the rental growth in the 
office and retail portfolio. DCCDL’s consolidated 
EBITDA stood at ` 5,718 crore in FY 2025-26 
in comparison to ` 4,949 crore in FY 2024-25, 
reflecting a 16% growth over the previous period. 
Total comprehensive income stood at ` 2,721 crore, 
reflecting a 11% growth over the previous year, 
which included an exceptional item of ` 489 crore 
on account of sale of Kolkata IT Park.
Review of Business
Development Business
The development business continued to deliver 
sustained performance with total new sales 
bookings for the fiscal at ` 20,143 crore.
The continued momentum in the development 
business was backed by successful launches of 
‘DLF Privana North’ in Gurugram and ‘The Westpark’ 
in Mumbai. DLF’s super luxury offering – ‘The Dahlias’ 
in Gurugram also continued to witness strong and 
sustained customer demand during the financial year.
Annuity Business
The annuity business performed well with robust 
earnings and continues to demonstrate steady 
growth and operate at a high occupancy level 
of 95%.
The retail business continued its growth trajectory 
by delivering 11% growth as compared to the 
previous year. All the retail malls continue to operate 
at high occupancy levels and deliver healthy growth. 
During the financial year, the business witnessed 
~0.37 million square meter (~4 million square feet) 
of new additions to the portfolio across Gurugram, 
Chennai and New Delhi.

Dividend
The Company continues to consistently reward 
its shareholders with a growing dividend payout. 
The Board has recommended a dividend of ` 8/- per 
equity share (400%) [previous year ` 6/- per equity 
share] of the face value of ` 2/- each for FY 2025-26, 
payable to those shareholders, whose names 
appear in the Register of Members/ list of Beneficial 
Owners, provided by the Depositories, on the 
record date. The recommended dividend reflect a 
year-on-year growth of 33%.
The total outgo on account of payment of dividend 
for FY 2025-26 would be ` 1,980.25 crore (previous 
year ` 1,485.19 crore).
Dividend payout is subject to the approval of 
members at the ensuing Annual General Meeting 
(‘AGM’) and shall also be subject to the deduction 
of tax at source.
The dividend payout is in accordance with the 
prevalent applicable laws and the Company’s 
Dividend Distribution Policy, pursuant to the 
provisions of Regulation 43A of the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, 
as amended (‘SEBI Listing Regulations’). The said 
Policy is available on the website of the Company 
at Dividend Distribution Policy.

capital of the Company during FY 2025-26.

transferred any amount to the general reserve.

1. ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
Global Economy
The global macro environment continued to face 
uncertainty, shaped by geopolitical tensions, 
elevated energy prices and tighter financial 
conditions. The International Monetary Fund 
projects global growth of 3.1% in 2026, underscoring 
a backdrop of moderate expansion and continued 
volatility in capital flows, inflation and trade.
Indian Economy 
India remained one of the fastest-growing major 
economies, continuing to outperform amid global 
uncertainty. According to National Statistical 
Office and Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation, real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 
is estimated at 7.6%. Inflation remained broadly 
contained, enabling a reduction in the policy rate to 
5.25%, while the Reserve Bank of India continues 
to monitor global volatility and commodity prices.

India’s residential real estate market remains in a 
structurally favourable upcycle, led by premium and

by urbanisation, infrastructure creation, rising 
household aspirations and an increasing preference 
for trusted developers with proven execution 
capability. For large and credible real estate players, 
the sector is seeing clear consolidation in favour of 
scale, brand and delivery track record.
New launches across the top seven cities stood 
at ~4,19,200 units in Calendar Year (CY) 2025, up 
2% year-on-year, while absorption was ~3,95,600 
units. Even with some moderation in volumes, 
overall sales value crossed ₹ 6 lakh crore, rising 6% 
year-on-year, reflecting sustained pricing power 
and a richer premium mix.
Premiumisation continued to shape new supply, 
with units priced above ₹ 1.5 crore, accounting for 
42% of total launches in CY 2025. This mix shift 
supports stronger monetisation, healthier project 
economics and sustained value creation for 
well-positioned developers.
The outlook for the residential sector remains 
positive with continued premiumisation and further 
consolidation towards credible brands, offering 
high quality products. 
b) Office Segment
India’s office market delivered a record year in 
CY 2025, with gross leasing of ~7.68 million square 
meter (msm) [~82.6 million square feet (msf)], the 
highest annual absorption on record and the third 
consecutive year of demand growth. The segment 
continues to offer a compelling annuity growth 
profile for owners of high-quality commercial 
portfolios.
Global Capability Centres (GCCs), technology 
companies, flex-space operators, Banking, 
Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) occupiers 
drove leasing demand, together accounting 
for ~60% of the total absorption in CY 2025. 
Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi-NCR contributed 
~61% of the total take-up. The underlying 
demand drivers continue to support rental growth, 
healthy occupancy and development visibility for 
institutional-grade office assets.
The office outlook remains constructive, supported by 
India’s cost competitiveness, deep talent base and rising 
GCC penetration. While geopolitical developments 
and the evolving impact of artificial intelligence 
warrant monitoring, demand for high-quality, 
future-ready workspaces is expected to remain 
strong, supporting long-duration annuity growth.
c) Retail Segment
India’s retail real estate market also recorded a 
strong CY 2025, with leasing activity reaching 
~0.83 msm (~8.9 msf). Consumption-led growth 
and premiumisation trends continue to support 
demand for high-quality retail destinations.
Leasing momentum was driven by experiential 
flagship formats and the continued physical 
expansion of direct-to-consumer brands and 
improving consumer demand.
Hyderabad, Mumbai and Delhi-NCR together 
accounted for ~65% of the total leasing activity 
during CY 2025. Fashion and apparel led category 
demand, accounting for 52% of absorption in 
Q4 2025, followed by food and beverage at 11% 
and homeware and furnishings at 6%, according to 
CBRE Research. 
The retail outlook remains positive, supported by 
rising consumption, premiumisation and sustained 
demand for investment-grade retail assets. For 
owners of quality portfolios, this should translate 
into resilient occupancy and steady rental growth.

profile.
